newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares trading weaker, correcting 1.3pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares trading weaker, correcting 1.3pct.

text.p: Greek shares continued to head south in early Friday trading on the back of a 1.92 percent drop on Thursday on rising interbank rates, a reaction to a softer drachma.
The one-month Athibor, the reference rate for Greece's interbank market, firmed 57 basis points to 11.50 percent on Thursday in relation to forex outflows.
Interbank rates were rangebound in early Friday deals.
Greece's central bank intervened at Thursday's fixing to prop up the drachma selling large amounts of ecus and marks and was expected to do so again on Friday if forex outflows picked up once more.
Market participants said they viewed the correction as a buying opportunity.
"Our investment targets have not changed and we treat the ongoing price correction as an excellent buying opportunity," said Michael Eleftheriou, fund manager at Alpha Mutual Funds."

"Nervousness is expected to prevail in today's trading session... We expect the positive news on the CPI front to improve market sentiment and any further stock price weakness should be viewed as a buying opportunity," said Telesis Securities in its daily outlook.
Press reports suggested that May CPI inflation might ease to as low as 5.1 - 5.2 percent from 5.9 percent in April.
Domestic investors remained bullish despite some foreign portfolio selling Greek equities on forex nervousness.
"Foreign short-term funds monitoring the market may have opted out on the first sign of a price weakness on Thursday," said Eleftheriou.
"But this year's rally has been mostly supported by retail investors who do not respond swiftly to changes in the macroeconomic environment."
Their decision to move out of the fixed-income area was based on the long-term prospect of falling inflation and interest rates, he added.
Moderate trading volumes suggested that there was no large scale selling in shares.
"Turnover figures for Thursday and early Friday are below the average for the recent period, indicating that there is no large-scale switch out of equities," Eleftheriou said.

The Athens general index was off 1.06 percent or 17.8 points to 1,665.00 from Thursday's 1,682.88 close after 30 minutes of trading, rebounding from a low of 1,655.36 recorded in the early stages of the session.
Turnover amounted to 4.4 billion on volume of 0.9 million shares.
Decliners beat advancers 93 to 63 with 15 shares unchanged on 171 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,109-1,139. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were flat at 6,900 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 698.05-742.60. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $88.31-$90.00. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 4,065-4,297 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $20.95-$22.65. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted lower at 295-329 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
